A24_REGISTRY_FALLBACK_SCOPE_RECORD.json.contradiction_statement: The amendment's registered enumeration ('exactly 3 debut games ... 6 rows total. No other row is affected') is measured FALSE on the real universe: the rule's own predicate (no prior contract-schedule game) is also structurally true for the four 2021 teams whose first contract game was 2021-05-15 (the archive begins 2021-05-14; an archive-start boundary fact, not a franchise debut). Measured: 7 own-side rows / 10 affected rows / 5 games. The RULE sentence is the operative frozen text (frozen-text precedence, the EXEC-M6 basis) and the only reading achieving the amendment's own registered purpose, 'extends the domain of rest(.,.) to a total function over the real universe'; the enumeration's error is REPORTED here and in EXECUTION_LOG.md, never silently reconciled.
A24_REGISTRY_FALLBACK_SCOPE_RECORD.json.rule_operative_text: FRANCHISE-DEBUT FALLBACK. For any team t and game g such that t has played no prior CONTRACT-SCHEDULE game before g (t's franchise-debut game), define rest(t,g) := cap (10) - the debuting team is treated as fully rested. This extends the domain of rest(.,.) to a total function over the real universe without altering its value on any row where a prior contract game exists. x(t,g) = (rest(t,g) + rest(opp(g,t),g))/2 is then computed unchanged by the frozen formula, using the extended rest(.,.). The rule applies identically whichever side of the row-pair the debuting team appears on (its own offensive row, or as opp(g,t) in its first opponent's row) - both rows of a debut game receive the identical resulting x. Affected rows: exactly 3 debut games (1611661331 vs its 2025 opponent; 1611661327 vs its 2026 opponent; 1611661332 vs its 2026 opponent) x 2 rows/game = 6 rows total (matches the auditor's measured >=6, including the fold-4/5 TEST rows for the two 2026 debuts). No other row is affected: only a team with zero prior contract-schedule games triggers the fallback, and each of the three named teams triggers it on exactly one game (its own debut).
